key_insight: This paper streamlines feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting by coding multi-view features directly, instead of first generating a full Gaussian scene and compressing it afterward. The result is a more end-to-end, differentiable pipeline that better fits efficient scene reconstruction and compression.
problem_solved: It addresses the inefficiency and complexity of existing feed-forward 3DGS pipelines that use a separate generate-then-compress workflow, often with non-differentiable steps and attribute-specific codecs for geometry and appearance.
method: Encode multi-view features in a feed-forward manner before full Gaussian generation.
Replace the separate geometry/appearance compression stages with a unified feature-coding pipeline.
Keep the reconstruction process differentiable and simpler for end-to-end learning.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means faster and cleaner 3D scene reconstruction from sparse views with less engineering overhead. It can simplify deployment of 3DGS systems by reducing reliance on handcrafted, non-differentiable compression modules.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing generate-then-compress vs. direct feature coding
Before-and-after block diagram of geometry and appearance encoding
Icons for multi-view images, compression, and end-to-end differentiation
paper_title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
paper_authors: Seungmi Choi, Ji-Hyoun Choi, Suhyun Jo, Tae-Gwon Park, Hui Yong Kim
